summary.text: Jim Costa is the Democratic incumbent for California's 21st District, a Fresno-area almond farmer who has served in the U.S. House since 2005. Before Congress he spent 24 years in the California Legislature. He is the ranking member of the House Agriculture Subcommittee on Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry.

paragraphs.text: Costa was born on April 13, 1952, in Fresno to a family of Portuguese descent: his grandparents came from the Azores and established a family dairy in Fresno's Kearney Park. He worked on the dairy while growing up and now farms almonds in the San Joaquin Valley.

He graduated from San Joaquin Memorial High School in 1970 and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from California State University, Fresno, in 1974. As a student he interned for Rep. B.F. Sisk. After graduating he worked as an aide to Rep. John Krebs and as chief of staff to Assemblyman Richard Lehman.

Costa was elected to the California State Assembly in 1978 at age 26, the youngest member of the Legislature at the time. He served in the Assembly until 1994 and in the State Senate from 1994 to 2002, where he chaired the Senate Agriculture Committee. He sponsored the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act in 1995 and served as president of the National Conference of State Legislatures in 2000-2001.

His official biography credits him with establishing the San Joaquin River Parkway and Conservancy and the San Joaquin Valley Air Pollution Control District, and with securing highway funding, including for a stretch of State Route 180 named the Senator Jim Costa Highway.

Costa won an open congressional seat in 2004 after Rep. Cal Dooley retired, defeating Republican state Sen. Roy Ashburn, 53.4 percent to 46.6 percent, and took office in January 2005. He has represented the 20th District (2005-2013), the 16th (2013-2023) and the 21st (2023-present). He sits on the House Agriculture Committee, where he is ranking member of the Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry Subcommittee, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee's Europe Subcommittee.

He co-founded the Congressional Crime Survivors and Justice Caucus and is a member of the Blue Dog Coalition, the New Democrat Coalition, the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and the Problem Solvers Caucus. His official biography also lists work on water infrastructure projects such as the Friant-Kern Canal and Sites Reservoir and on California high-speed rail.
